units.title: Introduction: Digital Signals, Logic Levels and the Clock
topics: Digital logic operations and integrated circuits
Advantages and applications of digital systems

sections.title: Digital logic operations and integrated circuits
Advantages and applications of digital systems

summary: Digital signals resist noise because they are decided by thresholds.
Logic levels have guaranteed bands and a forbidden zone; noise margin measures the safety.
Clocks are described by period, frequency, duty cycle and edges; setup and hold times limit speed.
ICs range from SSI gates to ULSI processors; CMOS is the dominant family.

units.title: Number Systems, Binary Arithmetic and Codes
topics: Why computers use binary and codes: eight reasons

sections.title: Why computers use binary and codes: eight reasons

summary: Any base converts through the place-value rule; hex and octal are compact binary.
2's complement lets one adder do addition and subtraction; watch for overflow.
Floating-point splits a number into sign, biased exponent and fraction.
Codes serve different goals: BCD for decimal displays, Gray for one-bit change, ASCII for text, parity and Hamming for error control.

sections.title: Implementing logic functions with multiplexers and decoders
Building a 16-to-1 multiplexer and a 1-to-16 demultiplexer
Logic gates built from passive and active elements
Where combinational circuits are used: eight applications

summary: Gates → Boolean algebra → minimal expressions (K-map) → standard building blocks.
NAND and NOR alone are enough for any circuit.
Adders chain into n-bit arithmetic; the same adder subtracts with XORs on B.
Decoders, encoders, multiplexers and demultiplexers route data; any function is one MUX or decoder plus gates.

units.title: Flip-Flops, Counters and Registers
topics: Applications of flip-flops, counters and registers: eight uses

sections.title: Applications of flip-flops, counters and registers: eight uses

summary: Flip-flops store one bit and change on a clock edge; JK toggles on 11, D delays, T toggles.
Excitation tables turn a wanted state change into flip-flop inputs.
Ripple counters are simple and slow; synchronous counters are fast and need design.
Counters count and divide frequency; registers store and shift words.

summary: An FSM is a state register plus next-state and output logic.
Mealy outputs react to the input directly; Moore outputs change only with the state.
State reduction and sensible assignment shrink the circuit.
Always check the unused states and test the design with a sample input stream.
